speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; please tell me, is your skin covered in blisters, or is it more scaly and red? Also, have you had any fever or difficulty feeding recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you; based on your description of the rash appearing just one day after birth, is the skin erythematous and pustular, or are there visible vesicles and crusting? I will also need to see the specific appearance of the lesions, so please provide the requested medical images. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Rash_Newborn

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Toxicum Neonatorum. The clinical presentation of a generalized erythematous maculopapular rash with pustules on an erythematous base, appearing shortly after birth and sparing the palms and soles, is classic for this benign condition. No further tests are required.
